findings.problem: The date spine is declared as a track on every template with no per-surface R8 class, reinstating the one-global-policy error R8's post-mortem exists to prevent.
findings.invariant: Every surface carrying the spine names its R8 class (rule REQUIRED or rule FORBIDDEN) and justifies it against R8's test, not by analogy.
findings.prescription: Carry the spine only where the reader tracks a value across a row or entry (/catalog, home feed, /frontier); reduce it to plain inline dates on the uniform link indexes.

findings.problem: The concept's whole first-read argument rides on an aria-hidden decorative track and on spacing; nothing in the text tells a reader that vertical distance means elapsed time.
findings.invariant: A reader who cannot see the spine (assistive tech, or the folded 390 state) still reaches cadence from text order and dates alone.
findings.prescription: Give the spine one digit-free legend inside the [data-derived] fence, or render the gap itself as a labelled derived value.

findings.problem: F-K12 is resolved for prose entries, but the packet never states the element order for model records without prose, which R-C explicitly allows to stay facts-first.
findings.invariant: The packet names the element order for /wiki/model/<entry> as well as for prose entries.
findings.prescription: State that model records keep facts-first and that the spine carries their timeline.

findings.problem: Proportional spacing clamped to eight row heights can push later feed items below the 390 fold on the one page the brief requires to lead with content.
findings.invariant: At 390 the home first viewport shows at least as many changed-feed items as the current capture.
findings.prescription: Cap the gap in the narrow layout, or fold to uniform spacing below 48rem.

diagnosis.strongest: HIER - the clearest single organising idea of the four: one shared spine with one meaning (elapsed time), applied consistently, with F-K12 resolved and S18's dead column filled rather than retired.
diagnosis.weakest: DENS - chrome is declared globally instead of per surface, and the only stated density control is a gap clamp with an eight-to-one range.
diagnosis.critical_issue: The site-wide spine is a single global chrome policy on a property R8 has already measured as surface-dependent; it is the defect shape the previous loop paid a forced-choice diagnostic to find.
diagnosis.highest_value_improvement: Assign an explicit R8 class per surface and let the spine appear only where a reader tracks a value across a row; that settles F-hier-1 and most of the relocation question.

downstream.weakness: Built as written, the spine will read as added chrome on the three link indexes and as insufficient signal on day-one data.
downstream.cause: The identity is committed to a channel (spacing) with almost no variation until snapshot history is deep, which known_risks[1] concedes.
downstream.recommendation: Build only if the finalist can show the spine on a surface whose data already varies; otherwise the flagship reads as blank rather than as cadence.
